candidates.draft_body:
Meqabyan (Ethiopian tradition) First Book of Meqabyan (Mäṣḥafä Mäqabyan I) (c. 600 AD)

'As David said, MEN ATE THE BREAD OF ANGELS' — direct citation of Psalm 78:25 LXX (ἄρτον ἀγγέλων ἔφαγεν ἄνθρωπος, 'the bread of angels man did eat'). Meqabyan reads the wilderness-manna typologically as ANGELIC-FOOD given to Israel — a reading preserved in Christian patristic and Jewish-Targumic tradition (cf. Wisdom 16:20 in the LXX/Apocrypha — 'thou feddest thine own people with angels' food'; Tg. Ps-J Exodus 16:15 expands the manna's angelic origin). The chapter develops a CONTRAST between the light-filled heavenly city awaiting good kings (vv. 8-10) and the Gehenna prepared for the wicked — anchoring the eschatological framework of 1 Mq's closing chapters.

Meqabyan (Ethiopian tradition) First Book of Meqabyan (Mäṣḥafä Mäqabyan I) (c. 600 AD)

LIGHT-FILLED HEAVENLY CITY for good-kings (paired with seed 33:1 manna-as-bread-of-angels). The chapter develops a CONTRAST between the light-filled-heavenly-city (vv. 8-10) awaiting righteous-kings and the GEHENNA prepared for the wicked. The light-filled-city imagery parallels: REVELATION 21:23 ('and the city had no need of the sun, neither of the moon, to shine in it: for the glory of God did lighten it, and the Lamb is the light thereof'); ISAIAH 60:19-20 (Zion's-eschatological-light); 1 ENOCH 25:5-7 + 51:1-5 (the city-of-the-righteous in the Watchers + Parables sections); 4 EZRA 7:88-99 (the seven-fold-glory of the righteous-dead). Meqabyan's distinctive contribution: the city is specifically reserved for RIGHTEOUS-KINGS (the chapter develops the royal-soteriology that pairs Ch 7's king's-duties + Ch 6's heavenly-palace-ekphrasis into a coherent Meqabyan ROYAL-ESCHATOLOGY).
